newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vedior over allotment option exercised.
newsitem.headline: Vedior over allotment option exercised.

text.p: Temporary employment group Vedior and retail firm Vendex said on Friday the option to take up an additional 2.5 million Vedior shares to cover over-allotments had been exercised by the banking syndicate.
A minority stake in Vedior was floated by Vendex International NV earlier this week.
The so-called "green shoe option" raises the number of Vedior shares which were sold to private and institutional investors in and outside the Netherlands to 19.2 million.
"The total proceeds of the sale of Vedior shares are 749.6 million guilders," Vedior and Vendex said in a statement.
Vedior said it will use the proceeds to take a 20.12 percent interest in Vedior Holding NV, the vehicle in which parent Vendex has grouped its services activities.
Vendex will use the money to redeem a major part of the loans it took up to pay for the recent takeover of French temp agency group BIS.
"The share issue secures both Vendex and Vedior a sound financial position for further profitable expansion," the two companies said.
Vedior started trading on the Amsterdam bourse on Thursday at 48.00 guilders, up from an issue price of 39.00, to close at 45.10. On Friday, the share rose by 1.50 guilders to 46.60.

Morgan Stanley Dean Witter is global coordinator and lead manager of the banking syndicate. ING Barings, ABN AMRO Rothschild and Paribas Capital Markets are co-leads and ING Barings is listing agent. Banque Nationale de Paris, BZW, Merrill Lynch, Rabobank Securities and UBS are co-managers.
